text: Hi, everybody.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Can you hear me?
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So my name is M Shreve, and I work at Automatic.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And if you're not aware of what Automatic is, we are the company behind WordPress.com and Tumblr and a number of other properties.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And we're a fully distributed company with over 1,400 people in 82 countries.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And I'm here today to talk about our approach to AI enablement and upskilling our organization to use all of these new tools and ways of working.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So our but is that you don't just get
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Good quality learning or work out of just handing people the tools.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: You need to give them real time to learn and experiment.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So what we've been doing is running these two-week enablement programs where we bring people in in person for a two-week immersive experience.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And the way that we do that is through 50% facilitated learning.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Through our learning and development team and our AI enablement team, we pull together workshop hosts from within the company to run workshops and hands-on activities.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And we'll look a bit at what that curriculum looks like shortly.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then 50% real project work.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we have folks bring in real work that they want to get done or a tool or dashboard that would help them in their day-to-day work.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Or these can also be creating new skills or MCPs to enable them to work faster outside of the program.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And another large part of this is encouraging peer sharing.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So sharing their own workflows to show kind of the art of what's possible.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And as they work throughout the two weeks, we also do a number of project demos at the end of each day.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we've ran three flavors of this, our main set being for engineers, where we go a lot more in-depth, getting into applied AI.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We've also experimented with cross-functional programs, with product engineering and design getting together in a room, and discussing kind of the future of how we all work together with these new tools.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then we've also extended into non-technical teams and run workshops with our finance group, our executive leadership team, and other functions as well.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So our engineering curriculum starts the first few days, covering the basics, skills, and how to create them, learning how to use MCPs and spectrum and development, as well as kind of the foundations of how to use AI responsibly and how to apply it in a way that's mindful.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then we start getting into deeper topics, creating MCPs for new functionality, getting into the hook system of Codex and Claude, and being able to extend the harness that way.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: up to autonomous agents and running routines and such in the background.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then we end on some different applied topics.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So again, Automatic is behind WordPress.com.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we normally run a workshop on applied WordPress AI and some of the cool features that are in WordPress core around AI.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: As well as being able to create your own personal assistant.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we really try to walk people from the foundations up into the ability to start creating these new things for themselves.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And one thing that we found out is you cannot just write this curriculum once.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: As we're all aware, AI is constantly changing from day to day, week to week.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: The top model might be different depending on the latest release.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we're constantly needing to update the curriculum and stay current to make sure when we are running these programs, we're teaching the right thing and we're not teaching six months out of date.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Another interesting part I wanted to highlight here is we have our own internal MCP server called Context Automatic, and this allows us to rapidly add new tooling sets for MCPs that might not exist or that we want to build our own governance and observability layers on.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And one of the cool things that I'll highlight shortly is some of the projects coming out of these cohorts is extending these abilities.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So as people go through, the capabilities compound and we're able to do more as a company because of that.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Another main focus of our program is that these aren't just a number of people that we're sending through.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We're also wanting each person we send through to be a multiplier within the company and extend our reach to the folks that we can't get to yet.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So, so far this year, we've ran seven of these cohorts of groups of about 45 people.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And we're aiming to get around 600 people through these programs by the end of the year, which is about two-thirds of our engineers, as well as some of those other focus areas that I highlighted at the beginning.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And we would like to equip all these people with ways of sharing their knowledge out and, again, extending our reach.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we've tackled this in a few different ways.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We are beginning a guides program, or I think other companies call this their champions program.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And what we want to do is extend our team's reach into other areas and have these
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: like top practitioners that we've identified within the company be able to help us out and continue spreading the knowledge.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Because we're distributed, we also have began these local AI get-togethers
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So people that have gone through the program are able to then run these little events within their regions and run workshops and will help support that as well.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And we've done about 10 of those so far in various different areas of the world.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And it's been exciting to see what some of these people that have gone through the program have gone on to do and teach.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We also organize these things called AI ride-alongs, and these are little workshops that we run
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Basically showing how you work, how you use a different tool.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Because what we found is seeing someone in your similar role or in a similar job to you, being able to see how they use it is a lot more easy to grasp than just talking about the concepts.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then we're also attempting to build a shared skill and MCP infrastructure.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So again, that context aid C system that I mentioned, but also encouraging people to create and share skills and build on top of each other's work so that we're all kind of building towards the same kind of platform.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then we have an always on help Slack channel where we also ask people that have gone through this program to help out and just kind of be available for anyone newer to working this way to have a place to come and ask questions at any point of the day.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So I'm going to share a few of the metrics that we've been tracking and improvement we've seen throughout the program.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: One of these is intentionality and just applying AI to your work in a more thoughtful way.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Maybe these people came in at the beginning just using it as a chat bot or, you know,
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Not fully using an agentic workflow.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So having people be a bit more intentional about how and when they apply AI.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Flow, which is like how well they're able to integrate AI into their workflows.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: If people feel as if they're able to use it in a way that makes sense for them and not just using it for AI's sake.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then the sharing part, again, is very important to us so that we can continue reaching other people in the company and kind of making everyone a teacher and an expert on these topics.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We also track individual lift on various metrics such as skills and custom commands, how comfortable they feel using and applying MCPs, and other topics like context management,
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And what we've seen from doing various surveys after the program, so we'll do one 72 hours after, 30 days after, and 90 days after, people will continue growing within those 90 days.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Being able to apply things more and like they've had more time to experiment and try things.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we're still seeing people like gain confidence and experience even once they've gone through the program.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So I wanted to highlight just a few of the things that folks have built just within the two weeks of the program.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: One of these is an agentic analytic system.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So WordPress has a e-commerce platform plugin called WooCommerce.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And some of the people that went through our program
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Created an agentic system for asking questions about your store and getting back answers.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: A number of folks that go through build on top of context AAC.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So one of our earlier cohorts, they wanted to be able to use some of these tools for support and build a Zendesk connector, which now we've had adopted through various teams throughout the company.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We built other providers in there that might not have a native MCP or, again, because we wanted to add additional observability there.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We've been building out our own agent skills directory.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: We don't prescribe a single tool, so folks are able to use Codex or Claude or any other number of tools, OpenCode, et cetera.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So we wanted to build our skills directory in a way that can be used across all of those.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And the whole skills directory actually came out as a project from one of these cohorts as well.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And then finally, another one I wanted to highlight here is guided admin support.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So during a help session, say you want to show someone exactly where something is within the dashboard, they built a tool using
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: Claude Code that allowed them to be able to guide and lead a session, highlight different parts of the screen.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And this actually came not from an engineer, but one of our support folks that felt a bit more comfortable after going through one of our programs.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: That is the end of my presentation, but the one takeaway that I wanted people to take from this is give people real time to actually experiment and learn.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: You can't just throw a bunch of tools at them and expect their way of working to change.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: You need to make space and give an environment for learning and make that like the star of whatever your education program is.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And I will be available for questions at our booth, which is the automatic booth right over on the other side near that stage and the swag pickup.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So I'll be there for a little bit after this talk if you want to talk about anything I talked about here or you'd like to hear more about how we're
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: How WordPress.com and WooCommerce are embracing AI with our official connections and MCPs.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: So please stop by the booth.
speaker: SPEAKER_00

text: And yeah, thank you.
speaker: SPEAKER_00
